title: Anatomy of an eyeris Object
text: preprocessing .asc EyeLink files eyeris, returned objects class eyeris, contain key components used throughout package’s backend. key components : file: original file path source .asc file block: block number time_orig: raw tracker time (ms) time_secs: normalized tracker time, starting 0 (seconds) eye_x: eye position x-coordinate eye_y: eye position y-coordinate eye: eye (Left Right) recorded data sourced hz: tracker sampling rate (hz) type: whether source data recorded using diameter area method pupil_raw: raw recorded pupil source data arbitrary units (.u.) ’ll notice preprocessing step run, new column added pupil_raw column; new columns follow structure subsequent step appended previous columns name (.e., pupil_raw_{previous steps}_{current_step}). illustrate: pupil_raw -> pupil_raw_deblink -> pupil_raw_deblink_detransient -> … events: list data frames containing trial event messages timestamps blinks: list data frames containing start/stop/durations blinks info: EyeLink EDF header data parsed data frame latest: internal tracker used assessing steps run far confounds: list data frames containing confounding variables preprocessing step (see: 📊 Summarize Confounds) params: detailed list steps run parameters passed step epoch_{name}: list data frames given epoched timeseries Now ’ve explained can expect see running eyeris glassbox() function, ’ll demonstrate glassbox() wrapper generally comprised terms steps defaults implemented.

what: I received this message… what does it mean and what should I do?
title: Complete Pupillometry Pipeline Walkthrough
text: (hopefully) shouldn’t encounter , , let us explain: Basically default setting communicating EyeLink machine filtering enabled either live-streamed data saved data EDF files. want filters ’s unclear low-pass filter specifications, conflicts assumption eyeris::detransient() use one-step difference compute threshold detecting large jumps pupil data (suggesting blinking artifacts). general, ’d like data raw possible can “cook” fresh. , data aren’t raw possible, need run eyeris without detransient step. skip detransient step, pass detransient = FALSE glassbox() call. skip detransient step within glassbox pipeline, pass detrend = TRUE glassbox().
code: ***WARNING: SOMETHING OUTRAGEOUS IS HAPPENING WITH YOUR PUPIL DATA!***   The median absolute deviation (MAD) of your pupil speed is 0.  This indicates a potential setup / hardware issue which has likely propogated   into your pupil recording. Most often, this is due to online filtering being   applied directly to your pupil data via the EyeLink Host PC.   WE DO NOT RECOMMEND USING ANY ONLINE AUTO FILTERING DURING YOUR DATA RECORDING.   ***ADDITIONAL INFO*** The default setting for communicating with the EyeLink  machine is to have filtering enabled on either live-streamed data or saved data   in EDF files.  We do not want these filters because:  (1) it is unclear how the EyeLink machine is specifying their low-pass filter,  and (2) it conflicts with an assumption here in `eyeris::detransient()` to use   one-step difference to compute a threshold for detecting large jumps in pupil   data (suggesting blinking or other artifacts).   ***GENERAL TIP***  You should aim to have your data as raw as possible so you can 'cook' it fresh!   ***WHAT TO DO NEXT***  If you would like to continue preprocessing your current pupil data file,  you should consider skipping the `eyeris::detransient()` step of the pipeline   altogether. Advanced users might consider additional testing by manually   passing in different `mad_thresh` override values into `eyeris::detransient()`   and then carefully assessing the consequences of any given override value on   the pupil data; however, this step is not recommended for most users.   PLEASE CONTINUE AT YOUR OWN RISK.

title: Building Your Own Custom Pipeline Extensions
code: winsorize_pupil <- function(x, prev_op, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99) {   vec <- x[[prev_op]]   q <- quantile(vec, probs = c(lower, upper), na.rm = TRUE)   vec[vec < q[1]] <- q[1]   vec[vec > q[2]] <- q[2]   vec }

what: Example C: Epoch with Subtractive Baselining
title: Extracting Data Epochs and Exporting Pupil Data
text: Use 1-second window "DELAY_STOP" baseline apply epoch data. example, ’re extracting 1-second epochs following "PROBE_START" event applying subtractive baseline correction. baseline computed 1-second window corresponding "DELAY_STOP" event. words, means pupil trace normalized subtracting average pupil size pre-probe delay period (.e., baseline period).
code: eye_1c <- eye |>   epoch(     events = "PROBE_START_{trial}",     limits = c(0, 1),     label = "probeEpochs",     calc_baseline = TRUE,     apply_baseline = TRUE,     baseline_type = "sub",     baseline_events = "DELAY_STOP_*",     baseline_period = c(-1, 0)   )

title: Flexible, Extensible, & Reproducible Pupillometry Preprocessing
text: Despite decades pupillometry research, many established packages workflows unfortunately lack design principles based (F)indability ()ccessbility ()nteroperability (R)eusability (FAIR) principles. eyeris, hand follows thoughtful design philosophy results intuitive, modular, performant, extensible pupillometry data preprocessing framework. Much design principles heavily inspired Nipype. eyeris also provides highly opinionated pipeline tonic phasic pupillometry preprocessing (inspired fMRIPrep). opinions product many hours discussions core members signal processing experts Stanford Memory Lab (Shawn Schwartz, Mingjian , Haopei Yang, Alice Xue, Anthony Wagner). eyeris also introduces BIDS-like structure organizing derivative (preprocessed) pupillometry data, well intuitive workflow inspecting preprocessed pupillometry epochs within beautiful, interactive HTML report files (see demonstration ⬇️)!

title: Save out pupil timeseries data in a BIDS-like structure — bidsify
text: eyeris object class eyeris derived load_asc(). save_all Logical flag indicating whether epochs saved subset . Defaults TRUE. epochs_list List epochs saved. Defaults NULL. merge_epochs Logical flag indicating whether epochs saved one file separate files. Defaults FLASE (merge). bids_dir Base bids_directory. participant_id BIDS subject ID. session_num BIDS session ID. task_name BIDS task ID. run_num BIDS run ID. single files without blocks (.e., runs), run_num specifies run file represents. However, files multiple recording blocks embedded within .asc file, parameter ignored blocks automatically numbered runs (block 1 = run-01, block 2 = run-02, etc.) order appeared/recorded. merge_runs Logical flag indicating whether multiple runs (either multiple recording blocks existing within .asc file (see ), manually specified) combined single output file. TRUE, adds 'run' column identify source run. Defaults FALSE (.e., separate files per block/run – standard BIDS-like-behavior). save_raw Logical flag indicating whether save_raw pupil data addition epoched data. Defaults TRUE. html_report Logical flag indicating whether save eyeris preprocessing summary report HTML file. Defaults TRUE. pdf_report Logical flag indicating whether save eyeris preprocessing summary report PDF file. Note, valid TeX distribution must already installed. Defaults FALSE. report_seed Random seed plots appear report. Defaults 0. See plot() detailed description. report_epoch_grouping_var_col String name grouping column use epoch--epoch diagnostic plots interactive rendered HTML report. Column name must exist (.e., custom grouping variable name set within metadata template epoch() call). Defaults "matched_event", epoched dataframes valid column name. disable epoch-level diagnostic plots, set NULL. verbose flag indicate whether print detailed logging messages. Defaults TRUE. Set False suppress messages current processing step run silently.

what: Remove pupil samples that are physiologically unlikely — detransient
title: Remove pupil samples that are physiologically unlikely — detransient
text: intended use method removing pupil samples emerge quickly physiologically expected. accomplished rejecting samples exceed "speed"-based threshold (.e., median absolute deviation sample--sample). threshold computed based constant n, defaults value 16.

title: Remove pupil samples that are physiologically unlikely — detransient
code: detransient(eyeris, n = 16, mad_thresh = NULL)

title: Remove pupil samples that are physiologically unlikely — detransient
text: eyeris object class eyeris derived load_asc(). n constant used compute median absolute deviation (MAD) threshold. mad_thresh Default NULL. parameter provides alternative options handling edge cases computed properties within detransient()  \(mad\_val\) \(median\_speed\) small. example, $$mad\_val = 0 \quad \text{} \quad median\_speed = 1,$$ , default multiplier \(n = 16\), $$mad\_thresh = median\_speed + (n \times mad\_val) = 1 + (16 \times 0) = 1.$$ situation, speed \(p_i \ge 1\) flagged transient, might overly sensitive. reduce sensitivity, two possible adjustments available: \(mad\_thresh = 1\), transient detection criterion modified $$p_i \ge mad\_thresh$$ $$p_i > mad\_thresh .$$ \(mad\_thresh\) small, user may manually adjust sensitivity supplying alternative threshold value directly via mad_thresh parameter.

title: Remove pupil samples that are physiologically unlikely — detransient

title: Remove pupil samples that are physiologically unlikely — detransient
text: function automatically called glassbox() default. needed, customize parameters detransient providing parameter list. Use glassbox(detransient = FALSE) disable step needed. Users prefer using glassbox() rather invoking function directly unless specific reason customize pipeline manually. Computed properties: pupil_speed: Compute speed pupil approximating derivative x (pupil) respect y (time) using finite differences. Let \(x = (x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n)\) \(y = (y_1, y_2, \dots, y_n)\) two numeric vectors \(n \ge 2\); , finite differences computed : $$\delta_i = \frac{x_{+1} - x_i}{y_{+1} - y_i},      \quad = 1, 2, \dots, n-1.$$ produces output vector \(p = (p_1, p_2, \dots, p_n)\) defined : first element: $$p_1 = |\delta_1|,$$ last element: $$p_n = |\delta_{n-1}|,$$ intermediate elements (\(= 2, 3, \dots, n-1\)): $$p_i = \max\{|\delta_{-1}|,\,|\delta_i|\}.$$ median_speed: median computed pupil_speed: $$median\_speed = median(p)$$ mad_val: median absolute deviation (MAD) pupil_speed median: $$mad\_val = median(|p - median\_speed|)$$ mad_thresh: threshold computed median speed MAD, using constant multiplier \(n\) (default value: 16): $$mad\_thresh = median\_speed + (n \times mad\_val)$$

title: Epoch (and baseline) pupil data based on custom event message structure — epoch
text: eyeris object class eyeris derived load_asc(). events Either (1) single string representing event message perform trial extraction around, using specified limits center epoch around limits (just grabs data epochs subsequent event string type); (2) vector containing start end event message strings – , limits ignored duration trial epoch number samples matched start end event message pair; (3) list 2 dataframes manually specify start/end event timestamp-message pairs pull raw timeseries data – , required raw timestamp event message provided following format: list( data.frame(time = c(...), msg = c(...)), # start events data.frame(time = c(...), msg = c(...)), # end events 1                                        # block number ) first data.frame indicates start event timestamp message string pairs, second data.frame indicates end event timestamp message string pairs. Additionally, manual epoching words 1 block time event-modes 2 3; thus, please sure explicitly indicate block number input list (examples, see well example #9 details). event-modes 1 2, way pass event message string must conform standardized protocol eyeris knows find events (optionally) parse included metadata tidy epoch data outputs. two primary choices: either () specify string followed * wildcard expression (e.g., "PROBE_START*), match messages "PROBE_START ..." (... referring potential metadata, trial number, stim file, etc.); (b) specify string using eyeris syntax: (e.g., "PROBE_{type}_{trial}"), match messages follow structure like "PROBE_START_1" "PROBE_STOP_1", generate two additional metadata columns: type trial, contain following values based two example strings: type: ('START', 'STOP'), trial: (1, 1). limits vector 2 values (start, end) seconds, indicating trial extraction occur centered around given start message string events parameter. label (optional) string can provide customize name resulting eyeris class object containing epoched data frame. left NULL (default), list item called epoch_xyz, xyz sanitized version original start event string provided matching. choose specify label , resulting list object name take form: epoch_label. Warning: label specified event message strings sanitize, may obtain strange-looking epoch list element output object (e.g., $epoch_, $epoch_nana, etc.). data still accessible within nested lists, however, avoid ambiguous list objects, recommend provide epoch label safe. baseline (New) single parameter controls baseline correction. Set TRUE calculate apply baseline correction, FALSE skip . replaces deprecated calc_baseline apply_baseline parameters. baseline_type Whether perform subtractive (sub) divisive (div) baseline correction. Defaults sub. baseline_events Similar events, baseline_events, can supply either (1) single string representing event message center baseline calculation around, indicated baseline_period; (2) single vector containing start end event message string – , baseline_period ignored duration baseline period mean calculated number samples matched start end event message pair, opposed specified fixed duration (described 1). Please note, providing list trial-level start/end message pairs (like events parameter) manually indicate unique start/end chunks baselining currently unsupported. Though, intend add feature later version eyeris, given likely heavily utilized / demand feature. baseline_period vector 2 values (start, end) seconds, indicating window data used perform baseline correction, centered around single string "start" message string provided baseline_events. , baseline_period ignored "start" "end" message string provided baseline_events argument. hz Data sampling rate. specified, use value contained within tracker's metadata. verbose flag indicate whether print detailed logging messages. Defaults TRUE. Set False suppress messages current processing step run silently. calc_baseline (Deprecated) Use baseline instead. apply_baseline (Deprecated) Use baseline instead.

what: eyeris: Flexible, Extensible, & Reproducible Pupillometry Preprocessing — eyeris-package
title: eyeris: Flexible, Extensible, & Reproducible Pupillometry Preprocessing — eyeris-package
text: Pupillometry offers non-invasive window mind used extensively psychophysiological readout arousal signals linked cognitive processes like attention, stress, emotional states [Clewett et al. (2020) doi:10.1038/s41467-020-17851-9 ; Kret & Sjak-Shie (2018) doi:10.3758/s13428-018-1075-y ; Strauch (2024) doi:10.1016/j.tins.2024.06.002 ]. Yet, despite decades pupillometry research, many established packages workflows date unfortunately lack design patterns based Findability, Accessibility, Interoperability, Reusability (FAIR) principles [see Wilkinson et al. (2016) doi:10.1038/sdata.2016.18 ]. 'eyeris', hand, follows design philosophy provides users intuitive, modular, performant, extensible pupillometry data preprocessing framework ---box. 'eyeris' introduces Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS)-like organization derivative (.e., preprocessed) pupillometry data well intuitive workflow inspecting preprocessed pupil epochs using interactive output report files [Esteban et al. (2019) doi:10.1038/s41592-018-0235-4 ; Gorgolewski et al. (2016) doi:10.1038/sdata.2016.44 ].

code: # first, define your custom data preprocessing function winsorize_pupil <- function(x, prev_op, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99) {   vec <- x[[prev_op]]   q <- quantile(vec, probs = c(lower, upper), na.rm = TRUE)   vec[vec < q[1]] <- q[1]   vec[vec > q[2]] <- q[2]   vec }  # second, construct your `pipeline_handler` method wrapper winsorize <- function(eyeris, lower = 0.01, upper = 0.99) {   pipeline_handler(     eyeris,     winsorize_pupil,     "winsorize",     lower = lower,     upper = upper   ) }  # and voilà, you can now connect your custom extension # directly into your custom `eyeris` pipeline definition! custom_eye <- system.file("extdata", "memory.asc", package = "eyeris") |>   eyeris::load_asc(block = "auto") |>   eyeris::deblink(extend = 50) |>   winsorize()  plot(custom_eye, seed = 1) #> !
